current.text: Cleveland has James Harden for a full season and added Peyton Watson. The projected starting lineup is Harden, Mitchell, Watson, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen.

With Harden on the team, Mitchell's assists, touches and usage dropped. His assists per 36 minutes fell from about 6.1 to about 5, his usage fell from 32 to 30, and his scoring fell by 1.5 to 2 points.
Much of last season's line came without Harden for about two thirds of the year, with Darius Garland missing or limited and Max Strus out.

Experts expect a smaller role this season. One projection has him just under 30% usage and about 33 minutes, and he could lose 20 to 25% of his assists next to Harden. Watson will also take some touches.

His two-point shooting last season was the best of his career. Experts expect it to regress, along with his steals. His free throw shooting late last season (about 93 to 95%) also propped up his value.
How much he plays with Harden decides his value. A hard stagger would help him keep it. Heavy shared minutes would hurt it. Cleveland's second unit has no clear point guard, so a stagger is possible.

Experts agree he is not a first-round pick this season. They call Yahoo rank 13 too high and ESPN's top-10 rank far too high. One expert would rank him slightly behind his Yahoo rank, and another ranks him 15th in 9-cat.
One expert would take Jamal Murray and Austin Reaves before him.
He went for 31 USD in an expert auction mock draft.
The expert called 31 USD about the right price for him.
He has no current injury concerns.
He dropped off later last season. Minutes and injury are both concerns this season.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league.
With a March 28 season end, Cleveland plays 4, 3 and 2 games in fantasy playoff weeks 19 to 21. The finals week, starting March 22, has only two games.
Cleveland is projected to win about 51 to 53 games. Coach Kenny Atkinson is under pressure.
He is signed to a contract extension.

durable.text: Points are his standout category. His threes, steals, FT% and assists are also clearly above the pool.
Turnovers are his weakest category for a guard. His blocks, rebounds and FG% are not strong.
Two-point percentage has always been his weak spot.
For most of his career he has been roughly a 30th to 40th ranked fantasy player. Last season was the only time he played at a first-round level.
He has had persistent knee problems, though he was fairly healthy last season.
He is 30 and has carried a heavy load over the last couple of years.

note: Every expert says Mitchell is not a first-round player this season. A full year of Harden should cut his usage and assists, and his two-point shooting and steals are expected to regress. Yahoo prices him at 44 USD (average cost 47.8) and ESPN at 59 USD, while our league paid 40 USD last season and an expert mock found 31 USD about right, so aim for roughly 31 to 40 USD and let others pay the ESPN price. He fits punt TO builds that want points, threes, steals and FT%. Early in the season, check how much he staggers with Harden, his assist rate, his steals and his two-point %. Also note that Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league and only two games in our finals week.
